item.title: Z.ai releases GLM 5.4 with looped transformer architecture
item.description:
Z.ai releases GLM 5.4 with looped transformer architecture

Z.ai has launched GLM 5.4, their first model to use a looped transformer architecture. This innovation allows for deeper networks without increasing the parameter count, making it more efficient for tasks requiring reasoning.

🔍 Overview

  • GLM 5.4 is a new model from Z.ai, featuring a looped transformer architecture.
  • It’s designed to be more efficient in tasks requiring reasoning, such as agentic coding.

🧩 How it works

  • In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass.
  • In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass.
  • Inkling 2 Mini, a looped transformer, runs the middle layers of the model three times for every token.

⚙️ Key details

  • GLM 5.4 is not yet available as open weights.
  • It can be accessed through the Z.ai API, which requires a Coding Plan subscription.
  • The API is OpenAI-compatible and can be accessed at https://api.z.ai/api/v1.

🚀 Availability

  • GLM 5.4 is currently only accessible through the Z.ai API with a Coding Plan subscription.

💡 Why it matters

  • The looped transformer architecture allows for more reasoning and can reach the right answer with fewer tokens.
  • This makes it particularly useful for tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality.

📊 Performance

  • GLM 5.4’s pelicans (a comparison metric) are more comparable to those from OpenAI or Anthropic models than previous generations.
  • The style transition between GLM 5.2 and 5.3 is stark, with 5.3 and 5.4 being more similar to OpenAI and Anthropic models.

📈 Comparison

Model Pelicans Quality Comparison to OpenAI/Anthropic Models
GLM 5.1 Different Radically different
GLM 5.2 Different Radically different
GLM 5.3 Similar Much more comparable
GLM 5.4 Similar Much more comparable

#AI #MachineLearning #Zai #GLM #LoopedTransformer

Source: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer

item.title: BitVLA: 1-bit Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotics
item.description:
BitVLA: 1-bit Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotics

BitVLA, a 1-bit Vision-Language-Action model for robotics manipulation, has been released. The official inference framework, robot.cpp, is now available, allowing for inference with I2S-quantized GGUF models without a Python or PyTorch runtime. BitVLA is accepted by CoRL 2026, Spotlight, and has achieved impressive performance metrics.

🔍 Overview

  • BitVLA is a 1-bit Vision-Language-Action model for robotics manipulation.
  • It is accepted by CoRL 2026, Spotlight.
  • The pre-trained BitVLA model has been released.

⚙️ Key details

  • BitVLA achieves 96.6% accuracy on various tasks.
  • It has a model size of 3.0B parameters and 1.4GB memory usage.
  • Inference with two-image LIBERO inputs takes 39 ms per action chunk on RTX 3090, approximately 9.7× faster than PyTorch eager and 5.4× faster than torch.compile.
  • On RTX 4090, it takes just 17 ms per action chunk (58.8 Hz).

🚀 Availability

  • The official inference framework, robot.cpp, is now available.
  • BitVLA can be run with I2S-quantized GGUF models without a Python or PyTorch inference runtime.

💡 Why it matters

  • BitVLA offers a more efficient and faster inference framework for robotics manipulation tasks.
  • It has achieved impressive performance metrics, making it a promising model for robotics applications.

#BitVLA #Robotics #AI #VisionLanguageAction #InferenceFramework

Source: ustcwhy/BitVLA

item.title: New Release 1.0.31: Enhancements and Fixes in AI Model Development
item.description:
New Release 1.0.31: Enhancements and Fixes in AI Model Development

🔍 Overview

The latest release, version 1.0.31, introduces several enhancements and fixes across various AI models, including ViT, EVA, BEiT, NaFlexViT, RepViT, and iFormer. These updates ensure normalization placement and distillation settings are preserved when exporting or reloading models after changing the classifier or pooling.

🧩 How it works

  • Fixes and Improvements:

    • reset_classifier() and checkpoint reconstruction fixes for multiple models.
    • Support for SwiGLU alignment in DINOv3 and Lingbot checkpoints.
    • Preservation of grayscale/non-RGB input channels in data loaders.
    • Layer-wise LR decay grouping fixes for RepViT, HGNet, MViTv2, and pre-norm ViTs.
    • InceptionNeXt feature sizes with output_stride=8/16.

  • New Features:

    • forward_intermediates() and prune_intermediate_layers() support for various models.
    • features_only support for CoaT, ConViT, ConvMixer, CrossViT, and Visformer.
    • prune_head=True removes the whole head, while prune_head=False keeps it.
    • Pruning a hierarchical model to an earlier stage removes the final norm and head sized for the last stage.
    • head_hidden_size is the actual pre-logits (pooled) width in all models.
    • Pool types a model can’t apply now raise at creation / reset instead of being silently ignored or failing in forward.
    • VOLO num_classes=0 output is the class token embedding.
    • Hyperparameter sweeps via a new sweep.py for grid/random search over any train.py argument.
    • WSD sweeps train one stable trunk per hyperparameter combination.
    • train.py enhancements for resuming, stopping, and saving epochs.
    • Add CSPNeXt with ImageNet-1k classification weights converted from OpenMMLab.
    • Foreach steps are chunked by device L2 cache size.
    • RMS update clipping for AdamWLegacy / NAdamW.
    • New decoupled/corrected weight decay NovoGrad variants.
    • Foreach (multi-tensor) impls for RMSpropTF, LaProp, LAMB, LARS, AdaBelief.

⚙️ Key details

  • Model Fixes:

    • reset_classifier() and checkpoint reconstruction fixes for ViT, EVA, BEiT, NaFlexViT, RepViT, and iFormer.
    • Unpooled PiT export and EfficientFormerV2 with distillation disabled.
    • NaFlex: fix ViT / EVA norm placement during conversion.
    • Layer-wise LR decay grouping for RepViT, HGNet, MViTv2, and pre-norm ViTs.
    • InceptionNeXt feature sizes with output_stride=8/16.

  • New Features:

    • forward_intermediates() and prune_intermediate_layers() support for CSPNet, NFNet, DLA, DenseNet, CoaT, ConViT, ConvMixer, CrossViT, HRNet, Inception-v3, Inception-ResNet-v2, NASNet, PNASNet, SelecSLS, SENet, Sequencer2d, VGG, Visformer, Xception, and Aligned Xception.
    • features_only support for CoaT, ConViT, ConvMixer, CrossViT, and Visformer.
    • prune_head=True removes the whole head.
    • prune_head=False keeps the head.
    • Pruning a hierarchical model to an earlier stage removes the final norm and head sized for the last stage.
    • head_hidden_size is the actual pre-logits (pooled) width in all models.
    • Pool types a model can’t apply now raise at creation / reset instead of being silently ignored or failing in forward.
    • VOLO num_classes=0 output is the class token embedding.
    • Hyperparameter sweeps via a new sweep.py for grid/random search over any train.py argument.
    • WSD sweeps train one stable trunk per hyperparameter combination.
    • train.py enhancements for resuming, stopping, and saving epochs.
    • Add CSPNeXt with ImageNet-1k classification weights converted from OpenMMLab.
    • Foreach steps are chunked by device L2 cache size.
    • RMS update clipping for AdamWLegacy / NAdamW.
    • New decoupled/corrected weight decay NovoGrad variants.
    • Foreach (multi-tensor) impls for RMSpropTF, LaProp, LAMB, LARS, AdaBelief.

🚀 Availability

  • Release 1.0.31 is now available with these enhancements and fixes.

💡 Why it matters

These updates ensure better model performance, stability, and flexibility, making it easier for developers to work with various AI models and configurations.

#AI #MachineLearning #ModelDevelopment #DeepLearning #ComputerVision

Source: huggingface/pytorch-image-models

item.title: Tabular Foundation Models Advance with Pretrained Transformers and Synthetic Data
item.description:
Tabular Foundation Models Advance with Pretrained Transformers and Synthetic Data

Open with one short intro paragraph stating what happened. Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) have emerged as a transformative approach to handling tabular data, leveraging pretrained transformer architectures to enable predictions on new datasets without task-specific training. These models, developed through synthetic data pretraining, eliminate the need for bespoke training pipelines while offering scalable solutions for complex data relationships.

🔍 Overview

  • TFMs are pretrained on synthetic datasets to infer variable relationships in unseen data.
  • They require no dataset-specific training, reducing overhead for maintaining custom models.
  • Prediction occurs via in-context learning (ICL), using a single forward pass with labeled rows as context.
  • Fine-tuning on specific datasets can further boost accuracy for critical use cases.

🧩 How it works

  • Input Handling: Specialized tokenizers map mixed data types (numerical, categorical, boolean) into a shared latent space.
  • Attention Mechanisms: Sequential row and column attention capture feature interactions but face scalability challenges.
  • Compression: TabICLv1 uses row compression (4 tokens per row) to reduce computational costs.
  • Pretraining: Synthetic data simulates real-world issues like missing values and outliers.

⚙️ Key details

Model Variant Contribution
TabPFNv2 First TFM to scale sequential row/column attention mechanisms.
TabICLv1 Introduced row compression for cost-effective cross-sample attention.
TabPFNv3, TabFM, KumoTabular Top-ranked models in benchmarks like TabArena, building on TabICLv1.
  • Synthetic data generation relies on Structural Causal Models but varies per TFM.
  • Computational costs grow rapidly with large datasets due to dense attention.

🚀 Availability

  • Integrated with Databricks workflows for managed GPU access and fine-tuning.
  • Check benchmarks like TabArena or TALENT for performance comparisons.

💡 Why it matters

  • Eliminates time-consuming model training and retraining cycles.
  • Enables rapid predictions via ICL without dataset-specific setup.
  • Advances transformer applications to tabular data, a historically under-explored domain.

#TabularData #AIModels #Transformers #SyntheticData

Source: Tabular foundation models on Databricks AI Runtime

item.title: Meta AI launches Muse Ember, a small, efficient reasoning model
item.description:
Meta AI launches Muse Ember, a small, efficient reasoning model

Meta AI just launched Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient model designed for complex reasoning execution and the work agents repeat all day.

🔍 Overview

  • Smallest and most efficient model in the Claude Haiku/GPT Luna category.
  • Targeted at tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing.

🧩 How it works

  • Offers six reasoning levels: minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, and max.
  • Visual examples include six pelicans riding bicycles, with the “max” level shown and others noted as comparable to Muse Wonder (40× the price of Ember).

⚙️ Key details

Model Input price (per M tokens) Output price (per M tokens) Token limit
Muse Ember $0.10 $0.50 Up to 1 M (price rises after a threshold)
GPT‑6 Luna $0.10 $0.50 Up to 1 M (price rises after a threshold)
Claude Haiku 5.5 $0.10 $0.50 Up to 1 M (price rises after a threshold)
Claude Fable 5.2 $8.00 $40.00 –
  • For shorter prompts Ember is priced the same as GPT‑6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5.
  • Pricing becomes less straightforward as prompts get longer; after the threshold Ember’s price sits between Luna/Haiku and Claude Fable.

📊 Efficiency metrics

  • Artificial Analysis is highlighted as a useful measure.
  • The Intelligence Index vs. Cost per Task chart places Muse Ember on the Pareto line, where improving one dimension requires sacrificing another.
  • Meta notes Ember sits on the efficiency frontier of the full Artificial Analysis leaderboard: no model scores higher for less per task.
  • The grey dot on the Pareto line (mid‑green area) represents GPT‑6.1 Terra (low), noted as worth attention.

🚀 Availability

  • Muse Ember is available now with pricing identical to GPT‑6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 for short inputs.
  • Longer prompts trigger a price threshold, positioning Ember’s cost between the low‑price models and the higher‑priced Claude Fable 5.2.

#MetaAI #MuseEmber #AIModels #Pricing #ArtificialAnalysis

Source: Introducing Our Smallest, Most Efficient Model: Muse Ember

item.title: NVIDIA releases RFD4-Proteina, an open BioNeMo model for joint protein sequence and structure design
item.description:
NVIDIA releases RFD4-Proteina, an open BioNeMo model for joint protein sequence and structure design

NVIDIA released RFD4-Proteina, an open BioNeMo model co-developed with the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design, that jointly designs protein sequences and all-atom structures using reward-guided inference-time search.

🔍 Overview

  • Co-developed with Institute for Protein Design at UW School of Medicine.
  • Uses patterns learned from nature to navigate protein design space.
  • Co-designs sequences and all-atom structures.
  • Employs reward-guided inference-time search to focus compute on promising candidates.

🧩 How it works

  • Combines explicit backbone coordinates with latent representation, learned sequence and atomistic variables.
  • Autoencoder decoder outputs sequence and all-atom structure together, removing need for separate inverse-folding step (e.g., ProteinMPNN).
  • During inference-time reasoning search, model denoises generation trajectories, scores designs, retains/branches promising partial states, continues until criteria met.
  • Rewards can measure geometry, interactions, or independent prediction confidence.
  • Uses residue-level latent representation (vs atom-level) to avoid memory blow-up.
  • Diffusion process engineered to cut sampling steps from ~400 (Proteina-Complexa) to ~60, focusing compute where reasoning matters.
  • Inference-time search accelerated via CUDA-accelerated oracles (OF3, physics methods like tmol).
  • Model and kernels co-designed with cuEquivariance and BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BIR) teams for speed/scalability.
  • AtomWorks provides molecular data layer for structure preparation and design annotations.

⚙️ Key details

  • Supports Linux GPU host, Python 3.12; follow repo setup guide, need supported NVIDIA GPU.
  • Self-host requirements: x86_64 or arm64 Linux meeting NIM prerequisites, Docker, NVIDIA Driver, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC API key.
  • NIM API endpoint (not for production): HTTP via build.nvidia.com, Shell/Python scripts, no local GPU/model install.
  • Accepts annotated CIFs or condition specification plus source structure.
  • Uses repository’s cropped PD-L1 structure from PDB 5O45 as target; fix sequence/backbone, allow side-chain repack, direct binder generation to hotspot atoms Tyr56, Met115, Tyr123.
  • Generated binder length 100–150 residues, free sequence and coordinates.
  • Install repo environment with current uv release (validated 0.12.24); update uv if present to recognize CUDA 13.2.
  • Setup caches Hugging Face model bundle including paired autoencoder.

🚀 Availability

  • Available as open model for training, inference, method development, direct control over sampling code.
  • Also available as NIM microservice for rapid inference deployment with HTTP interface.

💡 Why it matters

  • Faster and uses less memory than prior RFD3 due to residue-level latent representation, reduced diffusion steps, CUDA-accelerated oracles, and co-designed kernels.
  • Enables efficient protein binder design with integrated sequence-structure generation.

#ProteinDesign #BioNeMo #NVIDIA #DrugDiscovery

Source: Design Proteins with RFD4-Proteina Using Reward-Guided Inference-Time Search | NVIDIA Technical Blog
